deck.name: National Parks Trivia
deck.description: U.S. national parks, their landscapes, landmarks and natural history.

questions.prompt: Which U.S. national park was established in 1872 as the country's first national park?
questions.explanation: Congress created Yellowstone before Wyoming, Montana and Idaho became states.

questions.prompt: Which California national park contains Half Dome and El Capitan?
questions.explanation: Yosemite became a national park in 1890. El Capitan rises about 3,000 feet above the valley floor.

questions.prompt: Which river carved much of the Grand Canyon?
questions.explanation: The river carved the canyon over roughly the last 5 to 6 million years.

questions.prompt: In which state is Zion National Park?
questions.explanation: Zion was Utah's first national park, established in 1919.

questions.prompt: Which national park contains Delicate Arch?
questions.explanation: Arches has more than 2,000 documented natural stone arches.

questions.prompt: Which Utah park is especially known for its dense amphitheaters of hoodoos?
questions.explanation: Bryce Canyon is not a true canyon. It is a series of natural amphitheaters eroded into the edge of a plateau.

questions.prompt: Which national park protects much of the Waterpocket Fold?
questions.explanation: The Waterpocket Fold is a wrinkle in Earth's crust, called a monocline, nearly 100 miles long.

questions.prompt: In which state is Everglades National Park?
questions.explanation: The Everglades is the largest subtropical wilderness in the United States.

questions.prompt: Which national park protects Biscayne Bay and coral reefs near Miami?
questions.explanation: About 95% of Biscayne National Park is water.

questions.prompt: Which national park contains Fort Jefferson?
questions.explanation: Fort Jefferson is one of the largest brick forts in the Americas. It sits about 70 miles west of Key West and is reached only by boat or seaplane.

questions.prompt: In which state is Acadia National Park?
questions.explanation: Cadillac Mountain in Acadia is the first place in the U.S. to see sunrise for part of the year.

questions.prompt: Which national park is crossed by Skyline Drive?
questions.explanation: Blue Ridge Parkway is an NPS unit, but it is not designated a national park.

questions.prompt: Which pair of states shares Great Smoky Mountains National Park?
questions.explanation: Great Smoky Mountains is the most visited U.S. national park in most years.

questions.prompt: In which state is Mammoth Cave National Park?
questions.explanation: Mammoth Cave is the longest known cave system in the world, with more than 400 miles mapped.

questions.prompt: Crater Lake in Oregon fills what kind of volcanic feature?
questions.explanation: The caldera formed when Mount Mazama collapsed after a major eruption.

questions.prompt: Which Washington national park contains the Hoh Rain Forest?
questions.explanation: The Hoh is one of the largest temperate rain forests in the U.S. It gets about 12 feet of rain a year.

questions.prompt: What type of volcano is Mount Rainier?
questions.explanation: Mount Rainier is an active volcano. Its heavy glacier cover could feed large mudflows if it erupts.

questions.prompt: Which national park is crossed by Going-to-the-Sun Road?
questions.explanation: The road crosses the Continental Divide at Logan Pass.

questions.prompt: Which Colorado national park contains Trail Ridge Road?
questions.explanation: Trail Ridge Road is the highest continuous paved road in the U.S., reaching 12,183 feet.

questions.prompt: Which two deserts meet in Joshua Tree National Park?
questions.explanation: The Colorado Desert is part of the larger Sonoran Desert.

questions.prompt: Which Arizona national park protects giant cacti near Tucson?
questions.explanation: Organ Pipe Cactus is a national monument, not a national park.

questions.prompt: What gives Petrified Forest National Park its name?
questions.explanation: Over more than 200 million years, minerals such as quartz replaced the wood's tissue.

questions.prompt: Which national park contains the General Sherman Tree?
questions.explanation: General Sherman is the largest single-stem tree on Earth by volume.

questions.prompt: Which tree species is especially associated with Redwood National and State Parks?
questions.explanation: Coast redwoods are the tallest trees on Earth. The tallest known, Hyperion, is about 380 feet tall.

questions.prompt: In which state is Denali National Park and Preserve?
questions.explanation: The park's centerpiece, Denali, is North America's highest peak at 20,310 feet.

questions.prompt: Which national park protects the cliff dwellings at Cliff Palace?
questions.explanation: Chaco Culture is a national historical park, a different NPS designation.

questions.prompt: Yellowstone National Park lies entirely within Wyoming.
questions.explanation: Most of the park is in Wyoming, but it also extends into Montana and Idaho.

questions.prompt: Some U.S. national parks are outside the contiguous 48 states.
questions.explanation: National parks also exist in Alaska, Hawaii and U.S. territories.

questions.prompt: What is a hoodoo?
questions.answer: A tall, narrow rock spire shaped by weathering and erosion.
questions.explanation: Bryce Canyon in Utah has the largest concentration of hoodoos in the world.

questions.prompt: What is a caldera?
questions.answer: A large volcanic depression formed when the ground collapses after magma is withdrawn from below.
questions.explanation: Crater Lake in Oregon fills a caldera that formed when Mount Mazama collapsed about 7,700 years ago.

questions.prompt: Which national park contains Badwater Basin, the lowest point in North America?
questions.explanation: Badwater Basin is 282 feet (86 m) below sea level, in Death Valley National Park in California.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest U.S. national park by area?
questions.explanation: Wrangell–St. Elias in Alaska covers about 13.2 million acres, larger than Yellowstone, Yosemite and Switzerland combined.

questions.prompt: Mount Whitney, the highest peak in the contiguous United States, lies on the boundary of which national park?
questions.explanation: Mount Whitney (14,505 ft) is on Sequoia National Park's eastern boundary.

questions.prompt: Which national park protects Kīlauea and Mauna Loa?
questions.explanation: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park is on the Big Island. Haleakalā is on Maui.

questions.prompt: Which New Mexico national park contains a vast underground chamber called the Big Room?
questions.explanation: The Big Room is one of the largest cave chambers in North America. Large numbers of bats leave the cave at dusk in summer.

questions.prompt: Which national park protects the tallest sand dunes in North America?
questions.explanation: Star Dune in Great Sand Dunes National Park, Colorado, rises about 750 feet (230 m).

questions.prompt: The dunes of White Sands National Park are made mostly of gypsum.
questions.explanation: White Sands in New Mexico protects the world's largest gypsum dunefield.

questions.prompt: As of 2026, how many national parks does the United States have?
questions.explanation: There are 63. The newest, New River Gorge in West Virginia, became a national park in December 2020. The wider National Park System has 433 sites, including national monuments, battlefields and seashores.

questions.prompt: Which Utah national park is divided into districts called Island in the Sky, The Needles and The Maze?
questions.explanation: The Colorado and Green rivers split Canyonlands into these districts.

questions.prompt: Which Alaska national park is famous for brown bears catching salmon at Brooks Falls?
questions.explanation: Katmai's bears gather at Brooks Falls during the summer salmon run.

questions.prompt: Which national park is on the island of St. John in the Caribbean?
questions.explanation: Virgin Islands National Park covers much of St. John, including coral reefs and the ruins of sugar plantations.

questions.prompt: Which is the only national park in Ohio?
questions.explanation: Cuyahoga Valley, between Cleveland and Akron, became a national park in 2000.

questions.prompt: Which West Virginia park, known for whitewater rafting, was redesignated a national park in December 2020?
questions.explanation: New River Gorge was a national river before Congress made it a national park and preserve.

questions.prompt: Based on 2025 visitor counts, which was the most visited U.S. national park?
questions.explanation: Great Smoky Mountains recorded about 11.5 million recreation visits in 2025, more than twice as many as Zion, the next park. Entry is free, and the park is within a day's drive of much of the eastern U.S.

questions.prompt: Which South Dakota national park is known for eroded buttes, colorful rock layers and rich fossil beds?
questions.explanation: Badlands protects one of the world's richest fossil beds of ancient mammals, such as early horses and rhinos.

questions.prompt: Which North Dakota national park is named after a U.S. president who once ranched in the area?
questions.explanation: Theodore Roosevelt ranched in the Dakota Territory in the 1880s. As president, he protected about 230 million acres of public land.

questions.prompt: Which federal agency manages the U.S. national parks?
questions.explanation: The National Park Service is part of the Department of the Interior. The Forest Service belongs to the Department of Agriculture.

questions.prompt: In what year was the National Park Service created?
questions.explanation: President Woodrow Wilson signed the Organic Act on 25 August 1916, 44 years after Yellowstone became the first national park.

questions.prompt: Which national park protects five islands and kelp forests off the Southern California coast?
questions.explanation: Channel Islands National Park includes Anacapa, Santa Cruz, Santa Rosa, San Miguel and Santa Barbara islands.

questions.prompt: Which Texas national park sits along a great curve of the Rio Grande on the border with Mexico?
questions.explanation: Big Bend is named after the large bend the Rio Grande makes along the park's southern border.

questions.prompt: Which Wyoming national park is known for the jagged Teton Range rising above Jenny Lake?
questions.explanation: Grand Teton National Park lies just south of Yellowstone.

questions.prompt: Denali, in Denali National Park and Preserve, is the highest mountain in North America.
questions.explanation: Denali rises to 20,310 feet (6,190 m).

questions.prompt: Which national park had the second-most visits in 2025?
questions.explanation: Zion had about 4.9 million visits, just ahead of Yellowstone with 4.7 million. Grand Canyon placed fourth with 4.4 million, in the year the Dragon Bravo Fire closed its North Rim and destroyed the historic Grand Canyon Lodge.

questions.prompt: Which national park had the fewest visits in 2025?
questions.explanation: Kobuk Valley, in Arctic Alaska, had 7,786 visits. No roads lead to it, so most visitors fly in on small planes. Isle Royale in Michigan was the least visited park outside Alaska, with about 29,000.

questions.prompt: Which site in the National Park System had the most visits in 2025?
questions.explanation: The Blue Ridge Parkway, a 469-mile scenic road through Virginia and North Carolina, had about 16.5 million visits. Golden Gate National Recreation Area was second with 15.7 million, both ahead of every national park.

questions.prompt: About how many recreation visits did the National Park System record in 2025?
questions.explanation: That was 2.7% below the record of 331.8 million set in 2024. A 43-day government shutdown in October and November 2025 closed or limited many sites.

questions.prompt: As of 2026, which state has the most national parks?
questions.explanation: California has nine, including Yosemite, Death Valley and Channel Islands. Alaska has eight and Utah has five.

questions.prompt: Since 2026, how much does the America the Beautiful annual pass cost visitors who aren't U.S. residents?
questions.explanation: U.S. residents still pay $80. Nonresidents aged 16 and over also pay a $100 surcharge at 11 of the busiest parks, including Grand Canyon, Yellowstone and Yosemite.
